# Saint Seiya by Armor Class: A Manga-and-Anime Character Dossier

Saint Seiya’s armor hierarchy is meaningful but never absolute. Bronze Cloths are normally the lowest of Athena’s three ranks, Silver Cloths form the middle tier, and Gold Cloths are the elite guardians of Sanctuary; nevertheless, Cosmo, the Seventh or Eighth Sense, technique compatibility, armor condition, divine blood, and battlefield circumstances repeatedly allow a lower-ranked fighter to defeat or rival a higher-ranked one. The central Bronze Saints eventually reach Gold-comparable states and then God Cloths, while the strongest Marina Generals, Judges of Hell, and classic anime God Warriors can challenge Gold Saints under particular conditions. God Cloths are the clearest qualitative step above Gold Cloths, although even they do not make their wearers invulnerable.

The classic manga ends with Hades defeated, Athena saved, the Gold Saints sacrificed at the Wailing Wall, and Seiya struck by Hades’s sword. In the manga continuity he is left comatose and becomes the focus of *Next Dimension*; the Hades anime presents him as apparently dead. The classic anime adds the entire Asgard war, the Steel Saints, altered backstories, and several changed battles and fates. Its seven official God Robes are worn by eight combatants if the hidden Alcor warrior Bud is counted, an unresolved distinction that matters when comparing the Asgard roster.

## Roadmap

The analysis proceeds chronologically through the principal armor classes: Athena’s Bronze, Silver, and Gold Cloths; Poseidon’s Scales; Hades’s Surplices; and Odin’s anime-original God Robes. Each character entry identifies the armor or faction, power level, signature techniques, principal appearances and story arcs, continuity, and final fate. The final sections cover Steel Saints, Black Saints, God Cloths, selected later continuities, and the cross-class rules that make Saint Seiya’s power system more conditional than a simple rank ladder.

## 1. Scope, continuity, chronology, and armor taxonomy

### The continuities used here

Masami Kurumada’s original manga began in 1986 and ran through 1990, following five Bronze Saints through the Sanctuary, Poseidon, and Hades conflicts. The classic Toei television adaptation ran for 114 episodes from October 11, 1986, to April 1, 1989. Episodes 1–73 cover Sanctuary, episodes 74–99 are the anime-original Asgard arc, and episodes 100–114 adapt Poseidon. The Hades finale was later animated as a 31-episode OVA divided into Sanctuary, Inferno, and Elysion. The [classic chronology and episode list](https://en-wp.org/wiki/List_of_Saint_Seiya_episodes) and the [Toei television overview](http://wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Seiya_(TV_series)) provide the principal episode anchors.

| Label | Material | Narrative position | Adaptation status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Manga | Kurumada’s original series | Sanctuary, Poseidon, Hades | Primary continuity |
| Classic anime | TV episodes 1–114 | Sanctuary, anime-only Asgard, Poseidon | Manga adaptation with additions and changes |
| Hades anime | 31 OVAs, overall episodes 115–145 | Hades Sanctuary, Inferno, Elysion | Later adaptation of the manga finale |
| Films | Five classic films and later films | Usually outside regular chronology | Separate or contradictory continuities |
| Next Dimension | Kurumada’s official sequel/prequel | After Hades and the eighteenth-century Holy War | Direct continuation of the original manga |
| The Lost Canvas | Shiori Teshirogi’s separate Holy War story | 243 years before the original series | Separate continuity; anime incomplete |
| Episode G | Gold-Saint-focused prequel manga | Seven years before the original story | Separate spin-off continuity |
| Omega | Later anime continuity | About 25 years after the original anime | Sequel-oriented anime continuity |
| Soul of Gold | 13-episode anime spin-off | During the Inferno portion of the anime Hades story | Anime-original midquel |

The classic Hades OVA was released in three parts: 13 Sanctuary episodes, 12 Inferno episodes, and six Elysion episodes. From Inferno onward, the production staff and voice cast changed substantially, but the storyline remained an adaptation of Kurumada’s Hades material. The [Hades Chapter overview](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saint_Seiya:_The_Hades_Chapter) documents that three-part structure.

For manga-to-anime orientation, one secondary guide maps the TV Sanctuary material to manga chapters 1–45, Poseidon to chapters 46–95, and the unanimated continuation to chapter 96 onward. That correspondence is useful for navigation, but it is not a substitute for a complete chapter-by-chapter primary index. Where an exact manga chapter or volume is not given in the supplied references, the entry below labels the anchor as unavailable rather than inventing one.

### The armor system

Athena’s standard Cloth system contains 88 constellation armors: 48 Bronze, 24 Silver, 12 Gold, and four Cloths whose material or rank is unknown. Athena’s own God Cloth is treated as a separate divine armor outside that 88-piece inventory. The [Cloths reference](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Cloths) supplies those totals, while the [Saints overview](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Saints) emphasizes that Cloth rank is only a baseline: a Saint’s Cosmo, not the armor’s label alone, determines actual combat performance.

| Armor class | Principal faction | Typical function | Continuity |
|---|---|---|---|
| Bronze Cloths | Bronze Saints | Large support and expeditionary rank | Manga and classic anime |
| Silver Cloths | Silver Saints | Intermediate commanders and specialists | Manga and classic anime |
| Gold Cloths | Gold Saints | Twelve Zodiac guardians of Sanctuary | Manga and anime; later continuities add variants |
| Scales | Mariners and Marina Generals | Poseidon’s ocean army and seven pillar guardians | Manga and classic anime |
| Surplices | Specters | Hades’s 108-man Underworld army | Manga and Hades anime |
| God Robes | God Warriors | Odin’s Asgardian champions | Classic anime; separate Soul of Gold roster |
| Steel Cloths | Steel Saints | Technological support armor | Classic anime and Omega |
| Black Cloths | Black Saints | Inferior copies made by renegade Saints | Primarily manga and classic anime |
| God Cloths | Athena and selected Bronze Saints | Divine armor awakened by Athena’s blood and extreme Cosmo | Hades and later continuities |
| Divine Surplices/Kamui-related armor | Hades, Thanatos, Hypnos and gods | God-level protection, distinct from ordinary Surplices | Hades material |

Surplices are counterparts to Cloths, Scales, and God Robes, but they do not have an internal material hierarchy equivalent to Bronze, Silver, and Gold. Some are highly resistant while others are destroyed by comparatively simple attacks. Celestial and Terrestrial stars identify Specter categories, but the source material does not establish a dependable power ranking between them. The [Surplices reference](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Surplices) explicitly warns against treating star category or armor appearance as a universal durability scale.

### How power should be compared

The most useful comparison has several layers.

First comes the armor baseline. Bronze Saints are described as capable of roughly Mach 1 movement and 100 attacks per second; Silver Saints are generally two to five times stronger than Bronze Saints and can reach roughly Mach 5; Gold Saints who have mastered the Seventh Sense operate at light speed. These are narrative benchmarks rather than laboratory measurements. The [Bronze Saints](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Bronze_Saints), [Silver Saints](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Silver_Saints), and [Gold Saints](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Gold_Saints) references all qualify their class comparisons.

Second comes Cosmo. The Seventh Sense allows a Saint to perceive and generate power beyond ordinary sensory limits. The Eighth Sense, or Arayashiki, permits a living person to enter the Underworld without becoming an ordinary dead soul. A Bronze Saint who briefly reaches the Seventh Sense can therefore defeat an ordinary Silver or even Gold Saint, but that breakthrough is not necessarily a permanent class promotion.

Third comes armor condition. Athena’s blood repairs and strengthens the Bronze Cloths after Sanctuary, producing the “Golden Bronze” states in Poseidon. Later, Athena’s divine blood creates the Final Cloths in Hades and helps them survive the Hyperdimension. God Cloths are a further transformation, not simply ordinary Cloths painted gold.

Finally come technique and circumstance. A mental, spiritual, musical, or dimensional attack may bypass raw armor durability. Hades Castle reduces Athena’s Saints to one-tenth of their normal power while Rhadamanthys retains his strength. Yggdrasil drains Cosmo in *Soul of Gold* while empowering the God Warriors. A fight involving Athena’s blood, Libra weapons, a forbidden team technique, or a hostile environment cannot be treated as a neutral class comparison.

## 2. Cloths: Bronze Saints

### The Bronze class

Bronze Saints are Athena’s largest and formally lowest-ranking group. Their normal duties include reconnaissance, support, intelligence-gathering, and defense of civilians. The main five, however, repeatedly exceed the class baseline. Seiya, Shiryu, Hyoga, Shun, and Ikki all reach Silver- or Gold-comparable states through Cosmo, and all five eventually wear God Cloths in the Hades climax.

The original manga visibly presents ten Bronze Saints plus Chameleon Juné, while the anime and later reference lists show additional Bronze Saints. Because the complete 48-member Bronze roster is not individually depicted, the dossier below concentrates on every materially significant classic character and labels minor members whose techniques or later endpoints are unavailable.

### Pegasus Seiya

**Armor and role:** Seiya is the twentieth-century Pegasus Bronze Saint and the principal protagonist. He is the character through whom the series most clearly demonstrates that Bronze rank is not a fixed ceiling.

**Power level:** At the beginning he is a typical but unusually determined Bronze Saint. By Sanctuary he can briefly perceive and counter Gold-Saint attacks after awakening the Seventh Sense: he breaks one of Taurus Aldebaran’s horns and later contributes to the defeat of Gemini Saga. In Poseidon, his Pegasus Cloth has been revived with Gold-Saint blood; when his Cosmo reaches the Seventh Sense, it becomes almost as durable and powerful as a Gold Cloth. In Hades, the shattered Pegasus Cloth reacts to Seiya’s Cosmo and Athena’s blood to become a God Cloth, explicitly beyond Gold Cloths. That armor protects him from Thanatos’s attacks but does not prevent Hades from piercing his heart.

**Signature techniques:** Pegasus Ryūsei Ken, usually rendered Pegasus Meteor Fist; Pegasus Suisei Ken or Pegasus Comet Fist; Pegasus Rolling Crash; and, in the God Cloth stage, the strengthened True Pegasus Meteor Fist and True Pegasus Comet Fist. He also temporarily uses the Sagittarius Gold Cloth and its bow.

**Key appearances and anchors:** He earns the Pegasus Cloth by defeating Cassios with Pegasus Meteor Fist in classic anime episode 1. His Seventh Sense breakthrough against Aldebaran occupies episodes 42–44; the Saga confrontation concludes in episodes 71–73. He leads the anime-only Asgard battles in episodes 74–99, defeats Baian in episodes 101–103, and reaches the Hades climax in episodes 115–145. The manga anchor is the original Sanctuary, Poseidon, and Hades sequence; an exact chapter number is not supplied in the cited material. The [Pegasus Seiya profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Pegasus_Seiya) and [episode list](https://en-wp.org/wiki/List_of_Saint_Seiya_episodes) support these milestones.

**Final fate:** In the manga, Hades’s sword curses Seiya and leaves him comatose; *Next Dimension* begins with Athena’s attempt to save him. The Hades anime ends with Seiya apparently dead after Hades’s sword pierces him, while Shiryu, Hyoga, Shun, and Ikki carry his body away. The anime ending therefore supplies a more final visual image, but it does not erase the manga continuation.

### Dragon Shiryu

**Armor and role:** Shiryu wears the Dragon Bronze Cloth and is the disciplined martial artist of the group, trained by Dohko at the Five Ancient Peaks of Lushan. His Dragon Cloth is famous for its exceptionally durable shield and right fist; the reference describes them as “the strongest fist and shield.”

**Power level:** Shiryu’s early strength is unusually defensive. In the Galaxian War, his Rozan Rising Dragon and shield dominate Seiya until Seiya forces him to sacrifice both weapons for a fair fight. He reaches the Seventh Sense against Cancer Deathmask, recovering his sight in the process, and reaches the Eighth Sense in Hades. His strongest classic feats include cutting through Chrysaor Krishna’s Scale and Chakra points with Excalibur, surviving the Underworld, and helping awaken the Dragon God Cloth. He is a high-end Bronze Saint whose greatest power often appears when he accepts a self-destructive cost.

**Signature techniques:** Rozan Shōryūha, or Rozan Rising Dragon; Rozan Hyaku Ryūha, the One Hundred Dragons of Rozan; Excalibur, inherited through Capricorn Shura; and the forbidden Final Dragon, a mutual-destruction technique. His Libra Gold Cloth and Libra weapons are also central to his Poseidon and Hades performances.

**Key appearances and anchors:** His first manga appearance is chapter 4, “Galaxian War,” and his first complete anime appearance is episode 2. Episodes 4–5 cover his fight with Seiya; episodes 27–28 cover his blindness and defeat of Perseus Algol; episodes 48–50 cover Deathmask; episodes 65–67 cover Shura and Camus’s deaths; episodes 105–106 cover Krishna; and episodes 128–145 cover his Eighth Sense and Hades battles. The [Dragon Shiryu profile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dragon_Shiry%C5%AB) supplies the chapter 4 and episode 2 anchors.

**Final fate:** Shiryu survives the Hades war, delivers Athena’s Cloth, awakens the Dragon God Cloth, and helps defeat Hades. In *Next Dimension* he is identified as the future Libra Gold Saint succeeding Dohko. In the original-series *Omega* anime he is alive with Chunli and their son Ryūhō, temporarily loses his senses and Saint role after an unspecified accident, recovers, and later wears the Libra Cloth.

### Cygnus Hyoga

**Armor and role:** Hyoga is the Cygnus Bronze Saint, an ice-user whose Cosmo can reduce matter toward absolute zero. His emotional center is his devotion to his deceased mother and his complex relationship with his mentor.

**Power level:** Hyoga reaches Gold-comparable performance when he approaches absolute zero and awakens the Seventh Sense. His battle with Scorpio Milo ends with both Antares and Aurora Thunder Attack landing at nearly the same moment; Milo survives because of the Gold Cloth and recognizes that Hyoga would otherwise have killed him. Hyoga later reaches the Eighth Sense, receives a Final Cloth, survives the Hyperdimension because Athena’s blood protects it, and awakens the Cygnus God Cloth.

**Signature techniques:** Diamond Dust, Aurora Thunder Attack, and Aurora Execution. He also uses Freezing Coffin and the broader ice discipline associated with absolute zero. In the manga he is directly trained by Aquarius Camus. In the classic anime, the anime-original Crystal Saint trains him and is himself Camus’s disciple. This is one of the clearest differences between the two versions; the [manga–anime comparison](https://honeysanime.com/saint-seiya-anime-vs-manga/) documents the alteration.

**Key appearances and anchors:** Hyoga first appears in manga chapter 4 in shadow and is fully introduced in chapter 5; the anime introduces him in episodes 2–3. Episodes 47 and 59–67 cover Camus, Libra, Milo, and Hyoga’s Seventh Sense. Episodes 108–109 cover Kraken Isaac, while Hades episodes 128–145 follow his Eighth Sense and God Cloth progression. The manga also gives him an early role as a Sanctuary agent sent to assassinate the Bronze Saints; the anime replaces that opening with a more sympathetic introduction centered on Siberia and the Crystal Saint.

**Final fate:** Hyoga survives Hades and becomes the future Aquarius Gold Saint in *Next Dimension*. The classic anime and manga agree on his survival, but the mentor structure and parts of his early history differ.

### Andromeda Shun

**Armor and role:** Shun is the Andromeda Bronze Saint, trained in the manga by Silver Saint Cepheus Daidalos and in the anime by the renamed Albiore. His chains are both defensive and offensive, and his pacifism often conceals his actual power.

**Power level:** Shun is repeatedly described as potentially one of the strongest Bronze Saints, but he usually restrains himself because he does not want to kill. In Poseidon he defeats Scylla Io after using six improvised chain defenses and kills Io unintentionally. He defeats Sorrento with Nebula Storm but deliberately spares him. In Hades, Shun’s body becomes the vessel of Hades, meaning that his apparent “power increase” is not simply a Bronze-Saint transformation; it is the power of a god possessing him. After Athena’s blood separates Hades from his body, Shun returns to his own role and later briefly wears the Virgo Gold Cloth.

**Signature techniques:** Nebula Chain, Circle Chain, Rolling Defense, Thunder Wave, Nebula Stream, and Nebula Storm. The chain’s autonomous warning and ability to adapt to an opponent’s technique are as important as its raw force.

**Key appearances and anchors:** Shun defeats Jabu in episode 6 and Black Andromeda in episode 12. Episodes 103–105 cover Io; episodes 110–111 cover Sorrento; episodes 132–145 cover the Hades vessel revelation, Virgo Gold Cloth, and Andromeda God Cloth. The [Andromeda Shun reference](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Andromeda_Shun) documents his Hades-vessel role and Poseidon outcomes.

**Final fate:** Shun survives the destruction of Hades’s body and the Underworld. In *Next Dimension* he travels with Athena and the other Saints to the eighteenth century and is identified as the future Virgo successor to Shaka. His final classic fate is survival, though his body remains uniquely vulnerable to Hades’s recurring interest.

### Phoenix Ikki

**Armor and role:** Ikki is the Phoenix Bronze Saint and the oldest of the central five. He begins as the principal antagonist of the Black Saints arc, leading the Black Saints in an attempt to seize the Sagittarius Gold Cloth, but later becomes Athena’s most independent ally.

**Power level:** Ikki is stronger than most Silver Saints from the outset. His battle with Virgo Shaka is the clearest Bronze-versus-Gold comparison: Shaka removes Ikki’s first six senses with Tenbu Hōrin, but Ikki uses the deprivation to reach the Seventh Sense and briefly surpass Shaka. His apparent victory is suicidal, and Shaka later returns. Ikki reaches the Eighth Sense in Hades, defeats Garuda Aiacos, and briefly wears the Leo Gold Cloth in Elysion. His Phoenix Cloth’s capacity for rebirth gives him unusual resilience, but it does not mean every incarnation begins at the same power level.

**Signature techniques:** Phoenix Genma Ken or Phoenix Illusion Demon Fist; Hōyoku Tenshō, often Phoenix Wings Rise or Rising Phoenix; and the later Phoenix Flying or Flying Phoenix attack. His central combat method is psychological disruption followed by a concentrated Phoenix strike.

**Key appearances and anchors:** He first appears in episodes 6–7 as Shun’s apparently murderous brother and defeats Black Saints through episode 14. Episodes 54–58 cover his battle with Shaka. In Asgard, episodes 83–86 cover his victory over Mime without his Cloth. Episode 107 covers his defeat of Caça; episodes 132–134 cover Aiacos; and episodes 141–145 cover his escape from Cocytus, Phoenix God Cloth, and the battle with Hades. The [Phoenix Ikki profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Phoenix_Ikki) records the manga/anime differences in Saga’s and Kanon’s use of Galaxian Explosion.

**Final fate:** Ikki survives the Hades war and remains one of Athena’s active Saints. In *Next Dimension* he is proclaimed the future Leo successor to Aiolia. His repeated “deaths” are temporary defeats or sacrificial disappearances, not a final death.

### The other classic Bronze Saints

#### Unicorn Jabu

**Power level:** Jabu is a competent ordinary Bronze Saint who defeats Lionet Ban in the opening tournament and later protects Athena’s forces, but no reliable individual ranking places him near the central five after Sanctuary.

**Signature techniques:** No named technique is established in the cited material; his documented style is close-range Unicorn combat.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He fights Ban in episode 2, is quickly defeated by Ikki in episode 7, returns with the other minor Bronze Saints to protect Saori in episode 61, and appears alive at the Poseidon ending in episode 114. His manga chapter anchor is unavailable in the supplied references.

**Final fate:** He survives the classic anime. Later *Omega* gives him a customized Steel Cloth modeled on his former Bronze Cloth, but a complete later dossier is unavailable.

#### Hydra Ichi

**Power level:** Ichi is a lower-level Bronze Saint whose poison attacks trouble ordinary opponents but fail against Hyoga’s Cygnus Cloth.

**Signature techniques:** His Hydra-based regenerating poisonous claws and horns are documented; no separate named technique is supplied.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Hyoga defeats him with Diamond Dust in episode 3. He returns with Jabu, Ban, Nachi, and Geki to protect Athena in episode 61 and is alive at the end of episode 114. He also appears in Hades Sanctuary among the surviving minor Saints.

**Final fate:** He survives the classic material. His exact later fate and manga chapter anchor are unavailable.

#### Wolf Nachi

**Power level:** Nachi is a regular Bronze Saint defeated decisively by Ikki early in the story. His later value is defensive and organizational rather than exceptional combat power.

**Signature techniques:** No named technique is supplied in the cited material.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He is defeated by Ikki in episode 7, returns to defend Athena in episode 61, participates in the classic ending, and helps observe the Hades eclipse. His precise manga anchor is unavailable.

**Final fate:** He survives the classic anime and Hades-era aftermath. Later *Omega* gives the former Wolf Saint a customized Steel Cloth, but no full later power profile is supported here.

#### Bear Geki

**Power level:** Geki’s physical strength is his defining asset. He initially appears capable of strangling Seiya, but Seiya breaks his arms and defeats him by exploiting the source of that strength.

**Signature techniques:** Wrestling and constriction; no named special technique is supplied.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Seiya defeats him in episode 2. Geki returns with the other minor Bronze Saints in episode 61 and appears among the surviving defenders in episode 114.

**Final fate:** He survives the classic story. In *Omega* he becomes a Steel Saint with a customized Bear armor; the cited evidence does not provide a later numerical ranking.

#### Lionet Ban

**Power level:** Ban is an ordinary Bronze Saint and loses to Jabu in the opening tournament.

**Signature techniques:** No named technique is established by the cited sources.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His match with Jabu occurs in episode 2. He returns with the minor Saints in episode 61 and is alive at the Poseidon conclusion in episode 114.

**Final fate:** He survives the classic anime. Later *Omega* gives him a customized Steel Cloth modeled on Lionet, but the exact later arc and techniques are not retrieved.

#### Chameleon Juné

**Power level:** Juné is a Bronze Saint with a more specialized chain-based fighting style, but no reliable individual power ranking is supplied.

**Signature techniques:** Her Chameleon chain is documented; no named attack is established in the cited material.

**Key appearances and arcs:** She appears before the Sanctuary campaign as Shun’s friend from Andromeda Island and tries to warn him against the dangers of his training. In the anime she appears in episode 40 and helps establish the background of Albiore and the Andromeda trainees. The manga gives her a related role, but the exact chapter anchor is unavailable.

**Final fate:** She survives her known classic appearances. Her later endpoint is unavailable in the supplied evidence.

## 3. Cloths: Silver Saints

### The Silver class

Silver Saints wear the second-ranked Cloth class. A commonly cited baseline places the weakest Silver Saint at least twice as strong as a Bronze Saint, with the strongest ordinary members reaching roughly five times Bronze strength and Mach 5 speed. The category contains both ordinary middle-tier commanders and exceptional figures such as Lyra Orphée, whose power is repeatedly compared with Gold Saints.

The roster count is inconsistent. One classic Cloth list names 17 Silver Saints, while another overview gives 24 total and 16 active in the original story; a separate secondary page estimates approximately 24–28. These figures likely use different scopes, including later continuities and unshown Cloths. The [classic Silver roster](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Cloths) and [Silver Saints overview](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Silver_Saints) should therefore not be silently merged.

### Eagle Marin

**Armor and role:** Marin is the Eagle Silver Saint and Seiya’s teacher. She teaches him Cosmo, trains him in combat, and becomes one of Sanctuary’s most important independent allies.

**Power level:** Marin has no numerical rating, but her fight with Hound Asterion demonstrates high Silver-level tactical ability. By emptying her mind, she prevents Asterion’s telepathy from reading her movements and defeats him with Eagle Toe Flash. Her ability to survive Sanctuary missions and move through hostile territory places her above ordinary Silver fodder, although the supplied evidence does not establish Gold-Saint equivalence.

**Signature techniques:** Eagle Toe Flash and the empty-mind counter to Asterion’s Million Ghost Attack.

**Key appearances and arcs:** She trains Seiya before episode 1, appears in episodes 23–25 against Misty, Moses, and Asterion, enters Sanctuary during episodes 51–63, and assists in Asgard and Hades. The reference labels her confrontation with Shaina as anime-only. The anime’s Poseidon episode 106 temporarily presents Marin as Seiya’s sister, but Hades episodes 141–142 reveal the sister to be Seika instead; Marin’s true role is that of Seiya’s teacher and fellow seeker of a lost sibling.

**Final fate:** Marin survives the classic manga and anime conflicts. Her later Omega role is not fully covered by the supplied evidence.

### Ophiuchus Shaina

**Armor and role:** Shaina is the Ophiuchus Silver Saint, initially Seiya’s hostile rival and later one of Athena’s most loyal protectors.

**Power level:** Her early Thunder Claw overwhelms Seiya’s ordinary meteors and defeats him before he reaches the relevant Cosmo breakthrough. She is not consistently presented as a top Silver Saint, but her experience and aggression make her one of the most effective recurring Silver combatants.

**Signature techniques:** Thunder Claw and close-range claw attacks. Her greatest narrative weapon is persistence: she repeatedly returns after defeats and protects the Bronze Saints against stronger opponents.

**Key appearances and arcs:** She appears in the early Sanctuary material, fights Marin in an anime-original sequence, and participates in Asgard episodes 74–99. She reveals Syd’s hidden connection to Bud, protects the Bronze Saints from Bud, and carries the Libra Gold Cloth to Poseidon’s sanctuary in episode 103. She appears throughout Hades as a surviving Sanctuary defender.

**Final fate:** Shaina survives the classic story and remains close to Athena and Seiya. In *Omega* she remains an Ophiuchus Silver Saint and becomes Pegasus Kōga’s master. Her ultimate Omega fate is not stated in the supplied evidence. The [Shaina profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Ophiuchus_Shaina) supports her classic and Omega roles.

### Lizard Misty

**Armor and role:** Misty is the Lizard Silver Saint and the first major Silver opponent in the anime’s Silver-Saint campaign.

**Power level:** Misty is strong enough to dominate Seiya before Seiya discovers how to overcome his defense. His Air Shield and physical speed make him a clear ordinary-Bronze superior. His manga and anime portrayals differ enough that their feats should not be merged.

**Signature techniques:** Air Shield, a vibrating defensive barrier, and Mavrou Trippa, a violent wind swirl.

**Key appearances and arcs:** In the anime he fights Seiya in episodes 23–24 and is defeated by Pegasus Comet Fist and Pegasus Rolling Crash. The supplied secondary reference describes the manga version as killing Ikki during an initial encounter and destroying Mount Fuji, whereas the anime makes Misty the first Silver Saint to confront Seiya. He is later revived as a Hades Specter in episode 118 and defeated by Hyoga.

**Final fate:** Anime Misty dies in the Silver-Saint arc, is temporarily revived by Hades, and dies again. The manga endpoint is also death, but the opening battle differs. The [Silver-Saint character comparison](https://tvtropes.org/pmwiki/pmwiki.php/Characters/SaintSeiyaSilverSaints) records the adaptation distinction.

### Hound Asterion

**Armor and role:** Asterion is a Silver Saint specializing in mental perception and pursuit.

**Power level:** His mind-reading initially defeats Seiya by predicting every movement. Marin’s empty-mind technique neutralizes that advantage, demonstrating that Asterion’s strength is matchup-dependent rather than simply overwhelming.

**Signature techniques:** Million Ghost Attack. In the manga it is based on reading the opponent’s mind, anticipating movement, and striking pressure points. In the anime it is changed into a multiple-replica attack that fires a combined energy blast.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears with Moses in episodes 24–25. Marin defeats him but spares him in the manga so he can report what happened to the Pope. The anime has Marin kill him directly. A Hades tombstone bearing his name implies, but does not directly show, manga-continuity death.

**Final fate:** Anime Asterion dies during the Silver-Saint arc. Manga Asterion’s death is inferred rather than depicted. The exact manga chapter anchor is unavailable.

### Perseus Algol

**Armor and role:** Algol is the Perseus Silver Saint, guardian of the Medusa Shield.

**Power level:** His Medusa Shield is a technique-based threat capable of petrifying Seiya, Shun, and even Spartan. Shiryu can resist only because the Dragon Shield protects him; when that defense is lost, Shiryu blinds himself to avoid looking at Medusa and defeats Algol through heightened nonvisual perception.

**Signature techniques:** Medusa Shield and petrification through the shield’s gaze.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in episodes 26–28 and is killed by Shiryu after the Dragon Saint blinds himself. In Hades episode 116 he is revived as a Specter and killed again by Shiryu’s Rising Dragon.

**Final fate:** Dead in both the classic Silver arc and his Hades resurrection. The manga chapter anchor is unavailable in the supplied evidence.

### Lyra Orphée

**Armor and role:** Orphée is a legendary Lyra Silver Saint who becomes Hades’s musician. He is not a Specter and does not wear a Surplice, although his Hades role places him among the Underworld’s decisive combatants.

**Power level:** Orphée is explicitly compared with Gold Saints and is called the “Legendary Saint.” His music can incapacitate Bronze Saints and lull Pandora and the Three Judges. His strength lies in technique, emotional control, and the ability to affect multiple opponents at once.

**Signature techniques:** Stringer Nocturne, Stringer Fine, and Death Trip Serenade. His lyre can immobilize, induce sleep, and manipulate the battlefield.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears only in the Hades material, especially Inferno episodes 130–132. In the manga he performs for Hades every 13 days, attempts to smuggle Seiya and Shun into Giudecca, and plans to assassinate Hades.

**Final fate:** Rhadamanthys sees through his feigned sleep and pierces his chest. Orphée binds himself to the Judge and asks Seiya to attack both of them. He dies after enabling the Bronze Saints to reach Hades’s palace. The [Orphée account](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Wyvern_Rhadamanthys) and [Hades episode list](https://en-wp.org/wiki/List_of_Saint_Seiya_episodes) support this fate.

### The remaining named classic Silver Saints

#### Whale Moses

**Power level:** Moses is a conventional but dangerous Silver Saint, strong enough to defeat Marin with Asterion’s assistance and to overpower Seiya temporarily.

**Signature techniques:** His attacks are physical and maritime in theme; no reliably named technique is supplied in the cited material.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears with Asterion in episodes 24–25, uses Marin as bait, and is killed by Seiya after revealing information about Seiya’s missing sister. He is revived by Hades and defeated by Hyoga in episode 118.

**Final fate:** Dead in the Silver arc and dead again after Hades’s resurrection. Exact manga chapter anchor unavailable.

#### Crow Jamian

**Power level:** Jamian is a specialist rather than a straightforward powerhouse. His crow control and aerial mobility give him an advantage over an injured Seiya.

**Signature techniques:** Control of a flock of crows and aerial attacks; no separate named attack is established.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He kidnaps Saori in episodes 29–30. Seiya rescues her, and Athena’s Cosmo turns Jamian’s own birds against him; Shun finishes the fight.

**Final fate:** Dead in the classic anime. His exact manga chapter anchor is unavailable.

#### Centaurus Babel

**Power level:** Babel is a flame-oriented Silver Saint whose attack threatens the Bronze group but is overcome by Hyoga’s ice.

**Signature techniques:** Flame-based Cosmo attacks; no secure named technique is supplied.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears at the end of episode 25 and is defeated by Hyoga in episode 26. Hades revives him, and he is defeated by Hyoga again in episode 118.

**Final fate:** Dead in both versions of the conflict. Exact manga anchor unavailable.

#### Auriga Capella

**Power level:** Capella is a weapons specialist. His flying saucers force opponents to deal with attacks from multiple angles, but he is below Ikki’s level.

**Signature techniques:** His remote flying saucers and steel discs.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears with Dante in episode 31 and is killed by Ikki’s Phoenix Illusion, after which his own saucers slice him. Hades revives him in episode 116, where Shiryu kills him.

**Final fate:** Dead twice. Exact manga chapter anchor unavailable.

#### Cerberus Dante

**Power level:** Dante is a physically strong Silver Saint who uses chained steel balls, but he is exhausted after fighting Ikki and cannot withstand the combined Bronze assault.

**Signature techniques:** Steel Ball and Chain.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears with Capella in episode 31 and is finished by Shun after Ikki weakens him. He returns as a Hades Specter in episode 116 and is killed by Shiryu.

**Final fate:** Dead in both incarnations. Exact manga anchor unavailable.

#### Sagitta Ptolemy

**Power level:** Ptolemy is not among the strongest Silver Saints, but his deception makes him strategically decisive.

**Signature techniques:** Phantom Arrow, which creates multiple false arrows around one genuine arrow.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He guides the Bronze Saints into Sanctuary in episode 41 and strikes Athena with the real arrow. Seiya kills him, but the arrow creates the Twelve Houses crisis.

**Final fate:** Dead immediately after his mission. The manga chapter anchor is unavailable.

#### Canis Major Sirius, Heracles Algethi, and Musca Dio

**Power level:** These three are representative middle-tier Silver Saints. Their coordinated attack is dangerous to ordinary Bronze Saints but fails against Seiya wearing the Sagittarius Gold Cloth.

**Signature techniques:** Their individual named techniques are not securely supplied; their group combat and physical attacks are documented.

**Key appearances and arcs:** They attack Seiya in episode 37 and are killed simultaneously by the Sagittarius Cloth. Hades revives them, and Shun kills all three in episode 117.

**Final fate:** Dead in the Sanctuary campaign, revived, and killed again. Individual manga anchors unavailable.

#### Cepheus Daidalos and anime Cepheus Albiore

**Power level:** Daidalos is Shun’s manga master. The anime’s Albiore is described as a Silver Saint whose power is comparable to a Gold Saint, strong enough to make Milo struggle before Aphrodite’s poison creates an opening.

**Signature techniques:** No definitive named attack is supplied.

**Key appearances and arcs:** The manga uses Daidalos in Shun’s training history. The anime uses Albiore in the Andromeda Island flashback and identifies him as the master killed through Aphrodite and Milo’s intervention, discussed in episodes 40 and 69.

**Final fate:** Dead before the main Sanctuary assault. This is a major adaptation change in name, role presentation, and the extent of the character’s on-screen development.

#### Ara Nicole

**Power level:** Nicole is listed among the classic Silver Saints, but no individual feat or reliable ranking is supplied.

**Signature techniques:** Unavailable.

**Key appearances and arcs:** No materially developed classic appearance is established in the cited evidence.

**Final fate:** Unavailable.

## 4. Gold Cloths: the Twelve Houses and the elite Saints

### The Gold class

Gold Saints are Athena’s twelve Zodiac guardians and the highest standard rank among her mortal Saints. Mastery of the Seventh Sense gives them light-speed movement, and Gold Cloths are described as the most durable of the 88 standard Cloths. The armor is not entirely passive: Gold Cloths can respond to a wearer’s will, travel to distant places, and reject a morally corrupt wearer such as Deathmask. The [Gold Saints overview](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Gold_Saints) and [Gold Cloths reference](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Gold_Cloths) establish this framework.

Two equal Gold Saints can enter a Thousand Day War, a stalemate that may continue indefinitely or end with both dying. Three can combine their Cosmo into Athena Exclamation, a forbidden technique whose narrative energy is compared with a small Big Bang. That comparison is symbolic rather than a measured physical value.

There is no stable ordinal ranking among the Gold Saints. Shaka, Saga, Mu, Aiolia, Milo, Shura, Camus, and even Deathmask receive different “strongest” descriptions in secondary discussions. The most reliable conclusion is that the class is narrow enough for matchups, temperament, and technique to matter more than a fixed first-to-twelfth list.

### Aries Mū

**Armor and role:** Mū is the Aries Gold Saint, Jamir’s Cloth repairer, and one of the Bronze Saints’ most important allies.

**Power level:** The cited reference calls him the strongest raw psychic among living Gold Saints. He combines telekinesis, teleportation, Cloth repair, defensive barriers, and high-level attacks. His defeat of Papillon Myu is one of the clearest examples of a Gold Saint winning through technique and control rather than simple destructive force.

**Signature techniques:** Crystal Wall, Stardust Revolution, Starlight Extinction, Crystal Net, telekinesis, and teleportation.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He repairs Seiya’s and Shiryu’s Cloths before Sanctuary; guards Aries in episodes 42 and 73; defeats Myu in Hades episode 121; fights the Specters and Rhadamanthys in episodes 126–139; and appears with a God Cloth in *Soul of Gold*. The [Aries Mū profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Aries_M%C5%AB) identifies him as Cloth blacksmith and records his psychic specialization.

**Final fate:** Mū sacrifices himself with the other Gold Saints at the Wailing Wall. In *Soul of Gold* he is temporarily revived, fights the God Warriors and Loki, and survives that anime-original story.

### Aries Shion

**Armor and role:** Shion is Mū’s predecessor as Aries Saint, former Grand Pope, and survivor of the previous Holy War.

**Power level:** His duel with Dohko demonstrates that he is at least comparable to another legendary Gold Saint. In the Hades anime he uses Stardust Revolution and telekinesis against Dohko and Shiryu. His full-power placement relative to Saga or Shaka is not established.

**Signature techniques:** Stardust Revolution, Crystal Wall-related psychokinesis, and Cloth repair knowledge.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His death at Saga’s hands precedes the main story. He returns as a Hades Specter in episodes 115–126 and reveals the plan behind the revived Gold Saints. His exact manga chapter anchor is unavailable in the supplied references.

**Final fate:** Shion is restored long enough to awaken Athena’s Cloth and empower the Bronze Saints’ Final Cloths, then disappears when his borrowed life expires. He remains an important spiritual predecessor in *Next Dimension* and later continuities.

### Taurus Aldebaran

**Armor and role:** Aldebaran guards the House of Taurus and is the straightforward physical powerhouse among the Gold Saints.

**Power level:** His Great Horn overwhelms Seiya, Shiryu, Hyoga, and Shun until Seiya perceives the attack’s timing and breaks one horn. This does not mean Seiya is generally equal to Aldebaran; the victory depends on Seiya’s Seventh Sense breakthrough and Aldebaran’s willingness to honor the wager. Aldebaran’s death against Niobe is also a poor basis for ranking Niobe above him because he is deaf after his Poseidon encounter and is surprised by Deep Fragrance.

**Signature techniques:** Great Horn and the fast-draw combat posture associated with iai.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 42–44 cover his Twelve Houses battle. In the anime-only Asgard opening, Syd defeats him with a surprise attack; the later explanation says Syd and Aldebaran were otherwise evenly matched. Hades episode 117 shows Niobe’s delayed poison killing him. He returns at the Wailing Wall and later fights with a God Cloth in *Soul of Gold*.

**Final fate:** He dies in Hades, returns briefly to help destroy the Wailing Wall, and sacrifices himself again. In *Soul of Gold*, his God Cloth defeats Heracles, but Yggdrasil absorbs him during the collapse of Jotunheim. His ultimate spin-off resolution is anime-original.

### Gemini Saga

**Armor and role:** Saga becomes the false Pope after killing Shion and rules Sanctuary for thirteen years. His split between a compassionate side and an evil personality is the central political crisis of the original series.

**Power level:** Saga is consistently portrayed as one of the highest-end Gold Saints, but a fixed ranking above Kanon, Shaka, Mu, or Dohko is not securely established. His Galaxian Explosion can devastate other Gold-level opponents, his illusions control minds and space, and his Another Dimension can remove enemies from the battlefield.

**Signature techniques:** Galaxian Explosion, Another Dimension, and the Genrō Ken or Imperial Satanic Illusion. He also uses complex Gemini illusions that create a maze of light and darkness.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He is revealed as the false Pope in episodes 71–73. In the manga, Saga defeats Ikki with a second Galaxian Explosion; the classic anime delays Saga’s use of that technique and gives the first anime Galaxian Explosion against Ikki to Kanon. Saga returns as a Specter in Hades episodes 116–126 and uses Athena Exclamation with Shura and Camus. He appears in *Episode G* as Pope during the Titan crisis, where Galaxian Explosion seriously injures Cronos in that separate continuity.

**Final fate:** His evil side is destroyed after the Sanctuary battle, and Saga commits suicide by allowing Athena’s scepter to strike him. He later returns under Hades’s control, helps obtain Athena’s blood, and sacrifices himself at the Wailing Wall. *Soul of Gold* revives him temporarily; Loki defeats Saga, Mu, and Dohko even after their God Cloth Athena Exclamation.

### Gemini Kanon

**Armor and role:** Kanon is Saga’s younger twin. He first operates as Sea Dragon Kanon, a Marina General wearing a Scale, then becomes the Gemini Gold Saint after Saga’s death.

**Power level:** Kanon and Saga trained at roughly comparable levels, although the supplied reference describes Saga as more dedicated and somewhat stronger before the series. Kanon’s Galaxian Explosion is explicitly described as weaker than Saga’s, but he remains powerful enough to dominate lower Specters, mentally control Rhadamanthys, and defeat or outfight many high-level opponents. His inability to defeat Ikki in Poseidon shows that he is not automatically superior to every Bronze Saint.

**Signature techniques:** Genrō Ken, Genrō Maō Ken, Golden Triangle, Labyrinth of Twins, Galaxian Explosion, and astral projection.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He is revealed as Sea Dragon in episodes 110–114 and switches to the Gemini Gold Cloth in Hades episode 118. He fights Lune and Rhadamanthys in episodes 129–139. The [Kanon profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Gemini_Kanon) records that the manga has Kanon remove his Cloth and self-immolate with Rhadamanthys, while the anime adds a Galaxian Explosion clash and an anime-only soul appearance at the Wailing Wall.

**Final fate:** Kanon redeems himself, protects Athena from Poseidon, becomes the Gemini Gold Saint, and fights Hades’s army. He sacrifices himself to destroy Rhadamanthys. In the manga he takes Poseidon’s trident blow meant for Athena; the anime changes that moment so Seiya takes the hit.

### Cancer Deathmask

**Armor and role:** Deathmask is the Cancer Gold Saint and the most openly cruel of the Twelve Houses guardians.

**Power level:** He possesses Gold-level speed and a highly specialized soul attack, but he is generally treated as one of the weaker Gold Saints in direct combat. His greatest limitation is moral: the Cancer Gold Cloth abandons him because it rejects his cruelty. Shiryu’s victory is therefore both a Seventh Sense breakthrough and a demonstration that the Cloth no longer accepts Deathmask.

**Signature techniques:** Sekishiki Meikai Ha, the Praesepe Underworld Waves, which sends an opponent’s soul to Yomotsu Hirasaka; telekinesis and movement between the living world and the borderland of the dead.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He first fights Shiryu before the Twelve Houses, then confronts him in episodes 48–50. Hades episodes 115 and 139 return him as a Specter and later as a Gold-Saint soul. The [Deathmask profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Cancer_Deathmask) describes his manga Hades variation: he begs Rhadamanthys for his life rather than fighting him directly.

**Final fate:** Shiryu kills Deathmask after the Cancer Cloth rejects him. Hades revives him, but Shion’s plan reveals that the revived Gold Saints never truly betrayed Athena. Deathmask returns with his Cancer Cloth to help destroy the Wailing Wall. *Soul of Gold* gives him a redemption-focused revival in which he learns to value ordinary human life.

### Leo Aiolia

**Armor and role:** Aiolia is Aiolos’s younger brother and the Leo Gold Saint. His story is built around clearing his brother’s name and resisting Saga’s mind control.

**Power level:** Aiolia is an exceptionally direct offensive fighter. He participates in a Thousand Day War with Shaka, defeats five Specters with one Lightning Plasma in the Hades anime, and in *Episode G* uses Photon Burst to defeat the Titan Koios. These are strong feats, but they do not prove an absolute rank above every other Gold Saint.

**Signature techniques:** Lightning Bolt, Lightning Plasma, and the *Episode G*-specific Photon Burst.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 36–38 cover his confrontation with Seiya and his awakening from Saga’s Imperial Satanic Illusion. Episodes 51–53 cover his possessed battle and Cassios’s sacrifice. Hades episodes 122 and 126–139 show him fighting Specters, Rhadamanthys, and the Wailing Wall. The [Leo Aiolia profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Leo_Aiolia) identifies *Episode G* as a separate prequel continuity.

**Final fate:** Aiolia sacrifices himself with Mū and Milo at Hades Castle and later at the Wailing Wall. He is revived in *Soul of Gold*, awakens the Leo God Cloth, and becomes the story’s main Gold-Saint protagonist. His final anime-original fate is survival after the Loki conflict.

### Virgo Shaka

**Armor and role:** Shaka is the Virgo Gold Saint, Buddha’s reincarnation, and “the man closest to God.”

**Power level:** Shaka receives the strongest explicit qualitative descriptions among the Gold Saints: his Cosmo is called the most powerful of the Saints, and he is described as having complete control of the Eighth Sense. These statements should still be read alongside the Ikki battle, where a temporary Seventh Sense breakthrough allows Ikki to surpass him momentarily. Shaka’s strength is not just destructive output; it includes sensory deprivation, illusions, spiritual perception, and control of the Underworld threshold.

**Signature techniques:** Tenbu Hōrin, often Heaven’s Treasure; Rikudo Rinne or Six Worlds of Transmigration; defensive barriers; and spiritual projection through Arayashiki.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 54–58 cover his battle with Ikki. Hades episodes 121–125 cover his staged death at Athena Exclamation and his message written in blood. Episodes 137–139 show his return to the Wailing Wall. The [Virgo Shaka profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Virgo_Shaka) records his Eighth Sense and Hades role.

**Final fate:** Shaka’s body is destroyed by Athena Exclamation, but his spirit writes “Arayashiki” and reaches Athena. He later helps open the route to Elysion and sacrifices himself with the other Gold Saints. In *Soul of Gold*, his God Cloth defeats Baldr, although Baldr’s unexplained immortality complicates the fight.

### Libra Dohko

**Armor and role:** Dohko is the Libra Gold Saint, Shiryu’s master, and one of the only survivors of the previous Holy War.

**Power level:** His old-master persona conceals a fully capable Gold Saint. After releasing Athena’s Misopethamenos gift, he restores his youthful body and fights Shion on equal terms. His strength also includes access to the Libra Gold Cloth’s twelve weapons, although Athena and the Libra Saint must authorize their use.

**Signature techniques:** Rozan Hyaku Ryūha, the One Hundred Dragons of Rozan, and the Libra weapons.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears as Shiryu’s master throughout the early manga and anime, reveals his Gold identity in episode 39, and returns to active combat in Hades episodes 116 and 137–145. His exact original manga chapter anchor is unavailable in the supplied references.

**Final fate:** Dohko survives the Hades war and remains alive in *Next Dimension*. His Gold Cloth and spirit participate in the Wailing Wall sacrifice. *Soul of Gold* revives him, where he fights Utgardar and later faces Loki alongside Saga and Mū.

### Scorpio Milo

**Armor and role:** Milo guards the House of Scorpio and is one of Sanctuary’s most loyal but initially suspicious Gold Saints.

**Power level:** Milo’s speed and precision overwhelm Seiya and Shiryu. His Restriction fails against Hyoga because the Cygnus Saint’s ice protects his body, but Milo’s Scarlet Needle still nearly kills Hyoga. Milo admits defeat only after Hyoga freezes the fifteen Scorpio star points while launching Aurora Thunder Attack and Antares simultaneously.

**Signature techniques:** Restriction, Scarlet Needle, and Antares, the fifteenth and final Scarlet Needle.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 36, 40, and 60–62 cover his Sanctuary role and Hyoga battle. Hades episodes 118 and 126–139 show him testing Kanon, fighting at Hades Castle, and joining the Wailing Wall sacrifice. The [Scorpio Milo profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Scorpio_Milo) emphasizes the one-tenth power reduction at Hades Castle.

**Final fate:** Milo survives Sanctuary, is later reduced to one-tenth power and defeated by Rhadamanthys alongside Mū and Aiolia, and sacrifices himself at the Wailing Wall. He is revived in *Soul of Gold* and receives a Scorpio God Cloth.

### Sagittarius Aiolos

**Armor and role:** Aiolos is the Sagittarius Gold Saint, older brother of Aiolia, and the Saint who rescues baby Athena from Saga.

**Power level:** His most important feats are moral and symbolic rather than a long combat record. He escapes Sanctuary while mortally wounded, protects Athena, and later contributes his bow and Cosmo to destroy the Wailing Wall. His full individual ranking is unavailable.

**Signature techniques:** Sagittarius bow and Golden Arrow; the precise named attack list is not established in the supplied sources.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His death and testament drive Sanctuary. His spirit guides Seiya in episodes 37–38 and 63–64. Hades episodes 138–139 show his Gold Cloth and soul joining the other eleven. *Soul of Gold* revives him, but an episode leaves his fate unknown after Andreas overpowers him while Yggdrasil drains his Cosmo.

**Final fate:** Aiolos is dead in the original continuity but remains active through his spirit and Cloth. The *Soul of Gold* endpoint is explicitly unresolved in the supplied account.

### Capricorn Shura

**Armor and role:** Shura is the Capricorn Gold Saint, trained to regard himself as Athena’s most loyal warrior. He is responsible for mortally wounding Aiolos before later recognizing the truth.

**Power level:** Shura’s Excalibur can cut through Cloths and defensive structures, making him one of the class’s most lethal specialists. Shiryu can survive only by combining sacrifice, the Final Dragon, and Seventh Sense.

**Signature techniques:** Excalibur and the forbidden Final Dragon counter used by Shiryu; Shura’s own precise Excalibur attacks are his defining weapon.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 65–66 cover his battle with Shiryu and death. Hades episodes 116–126 show him as a revived Specter, and episodes 138–139 show his sacrifice at the Wailing Wall. In *Soul of Gold*, his spirit and Cosmo influence the Camus–Surt conflict.

**Final fate:** Shura dies after lending his Gold Cloth and power to Shiryu, returns under Hades’s apparent command, reveals his true loyalty, and dies again at the Wailing Wall.

### Aquarius Camus

**Armor and role:** Camus is the Aquarius Gold Saint and Hyoga’s direct master in the manga or grandmaster through Crystal in the classic anime.

**Power level:** Camus is one of the strongest ice users in the series. He freezes Hyoga in a Freezing Coffin to force him toward the Seventh Sense and reaches absolute-zero conditions in their final duel. His power is close enough to Hyoga’s that both attacks destroy their Cloths and kill Camus.

**Signature techniques:** Aurora Execution, Diamond Dust, Freezing Coffin, and absolute-zero ice manipulation.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 47, 59, and 67 cover his Libra and Aquarius battles with Hyoga. Hades episodes 116–126 show his Specter disguise, while episodes 138–139 show his return and sacrifice. *Soul of Gold* makes Camus a central figure because of his childhood relationship with Surt.

**Final fate:** Camus dies in the Sanctuary arc, returns in Hades to help Athena’s Cloth awaken, and sacrifices himself at the Wailing Wall. In *Soul of Gold* he is revived, temporarily appears to side with Surt, defeats Surt with Aquarius God Cloth, and survives the anime-original conflict.

### Pisces Aphrodite

**Armor and role:** Aphrodite guards the House of Pisces and is the assassin whose poisoned rose helps Milo defeat anime Albiore.

**Power level:** He is a high-end specialist whose attacks can kill a stronger opponent through poison, blood loss, or sensory impairment. His defeat by Shun is not evidence that Pisces is generally weak; Shun reaches the Seventh Sense and uses Nebula Storm while dying from Bloody Rose.

**Signature techniques:** Royal Demon Rose, Piranhan Rose, and Bloody Rose.

**Key appearances and arcs:** Episodes 68–70 cover his battle with Shun. Hades episodes 115–116 return him as a Specter, and episodes 138–139 show him helping the Gold Saints destroy the Wailing Wall. His *Soul of Gold* role is anime-original: he survives apparent absorption by Yggdrasil because he is immune to its plant poisons and secretly protects the other Gold Saints.

**Final fate:** Shun kills Aphrodite in Sanctuary. Hades revives him, and his loyalty to Athena becomes explicit at the Wailing Wall. *Soul of Gold* gives him an additional survival and support role.

### Gold-Saint outcomes and the Twelve Houses

Five Gold Saints die directly in the Twelve Houses conflict: Saga, Deathmask, Shura, Camus, and Aphrodite. Aldebaran later dies against Niobe; the remaining Gold Saints sacrifice themselves at the Wailing Wall. Poseidon’s arc largely keeps the surviving Gold Saints in Sanctuary on Dohko’s orders, although Gold Cloths and Libra weapons are sent to assist the Bronze Saints. In Hades, all twelve Gold Cloths and their souls gather to destroy the Wailing Wall, after which the Gold Saints are dead again.

The apparent contradiction between “twelve Gold Saints” and lists of fourteen named classic users is chronological: Shion and Kanon occupy Gold positions in different periods, while Aiolos and Saga belong to successive Sagittarius and Gemini eras. A separate *Next Dimension* development introduces the apparently thirteenth Ophiuchus Gold Cloth of Asclepios, but that inventory is continuity-specific and qualified as uncertain by the cited reference.

## 5. Scales: Marina Generals and Poseidon’s faction

### The Scale hierarchy

Poseidon’s Mariners wear Scales. Seven Marina Generals are assigned to seven ocean Pillars sustaining the Underwater Sanctuary and the seas above it. The classic order is Sea Horse Baian, Scylla Io, Chrysaor Krishna, Limnade Caça, Kraken Isaac, Siren Sorrento, and Sea Dragon Kanon. The [Mariners overview](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Mariners) and [Poseidon reference](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Poseidon) map each General to an ocean region and pillar.

The class is generally presented as Gold-comparable, but individual results are highly conditional. Baian receives a direct comparison with Gold Saints, Krishna requires a Seventh Sense and Excalibur breakthrough, and Sorrento’s music bypasses normal defenses. The General’s role as pillar guardian also means that an opponent may need to defeat both the warrior and an extraordinarily durable Pillar.

### Sea Horse Baian

**Armor and role:** Baian wears the Sea Horse Scale and guards the North Pacific Mammoth Pillar.

**Power level:** Seiya initially assesses Baian as equal to or stronger than a Gold Saint. This is a conditional narrative assessment, not proof that every General exceeds every Gold Saint. Baian’s invisible air-current barrier initially stops Seiya’s attacks, but Seiya recognizes it because it resembles Misty’s Air Shield.

**Signature techniques:** God Breath, Rising Billows, and the invisible air-current barrier.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Poseidon manga volumes 14–15 and anime episodes 101–103. His battle is one of the clearest cases in which prior experience with a Silver Saint supplies the tactical key to defeating a Marina General.

**Final fate:** Seiya’s Gold-blood-enhanced Pegasus Cloth breaks through the barrier, and Pegasus Comet Fist kills Baian. Seiya then requires the Libra Shield to destroy the North Pacific Pillar.

### Scylla Io

**Armor and role:** Io wears the Scylla Scale and guards the South Pacific Pillar.

**Power level:** Io is a versatile, high-end General who can cycle through six beast forms and attack a defensive specialist from multiple angles. He is eventually overcome because Shun adapts his chain to each form and reaches the Seventh Sense.

**Signature techniques:** Eagle Clutch, Wolf’s Fang, Queen Bee’s Stinger, Serpent Strangler, Vampire Inhale, Grizzly Slap, and Big Tornado. Shun counters with Spider Net, Casting Net, Spiral Duct, Boomerang Shot, Wild Trap, and Great Capture.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His full fight with Shun occupies anime episodes 103–105 and the corresponding Poseidon manga sequence.

**Final fate:** Shun defeats Io, breaks the Scylla Scale, and destroys the Pillar with a Libra weapon. Io sacrifices himself attempting to protect it.

### Chrysaor Krishna

**Armor and role:** Krishna wears the Chrysaor Scale and guards the Indian Ocean Pillar.

**Power level:** Krishna initially dominates Shiryu with his Golden Lance and a Chakra-based defensive field. His power is not simply a matter of Scale durability; the seven vital points of Chakra create a barrier that must be understood and severed.

**Signature techniques:** Golden Lance, Maha Roshini, Kundalini/Chakra defense, and the seven vital points that sustain his barrier.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His fight with Shiryu appears in anime episodes 105–106 and in manga volume 16. Shiryu first fails with the Dragon Shield, then uses Shura’s Excalibur to cut the lance, Scale, and Chakra points.

**Final fate:** Shiryu kills Krishna after awakening the Seventh Sense and destroys the Indian Ocean Pillar with a Libra weapon. The anime intervention is described as substantially identical to the manga.

### Limnade Caça

**Armor and role:** Caça wears the Limnade Scale and guards the Antarctic Pillar.

**Power level:** Caça is a psychological specialist rather than a straightforward powerhouse. He reads emotional memories and appears as people whom his enemies love. His technique defeats Seiya, Hyoga, and Shun through deception, but it cannot actually copy their attacks.

**Signature techniques:** Heart-reading transformations, Salamander Shock, and emotional illusion.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in anime episode 107 and the corresponding manga battle. He imitates Seiya’s sister Seika, Hyoga’s Camus, Shun’s Ikki, and finally Ikki himself.

**Final fate:** Ikki sees through the deception, defeats him with Phoenix techniques, and kills him with a strike to the heart. Manga and anime outcomes are substantially the same.

### Kraken Isaac

**Armor and role:** Isaac wears the Kraken Scale and guards the Arctic Pillar. He was Hyoga’s childhood training partner before becoming a Marina General.

**Power level:** Isaac is close enough to Hyoga in ice combat to make the battle emotionally and technically difficult, but Hyoga’s mature Seventh Sense and Aurora Execution eventually surpass him.

**Signature techniques:** Aurora Borealis, ice manipulation, and the Kraken’s freezing attacks.

**Key appearances and arcs:** His history and battle occupy anime episodes 108–109. The source describes his left eye being injured while rescuing Hyoga from the Siberian ice, after which he becomes disillusioned and joins Poseidon.

**Final fate:** Hyoga defeats Isaac with Aurora Execution. Isaac accepts Hyoga’s growth, warns him that Kanon initiated the war, and dies. Exact manga chapter anchor unavailable.

### Siren Sorrento

**Armor and role:** Sorrento wears the Siren Scale and guards the South Atlantic Pillar. He is also the General with the most important adaptation change.

**Power level:** Sorrento’s Dead End Symphony attacks the opponent’s Cosmo directly through the brain, bypassing Shun’s Rolling Defense and chains. Its effect continues even after the victim damages or blocks his ears. This makes Sorrento a technique-based threat whose matchup can be more important than conventional durability.

**Signature techniques:** Dead End Symphony and Dead End Climax.

**Key appearances and arcs:** In the manga, Sorrento first confronts Taurus Aldebaran after the Sanctuary chapter. In the anime, he first appears at the end of Asgard as Poseidon’s messenger, gives Hilda the Nibelungen Ring, fights Siegfried, and later returns in Poseidon episodes 110–114. The [Sorrento profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Siren_Sorrento) explicitly distinguishes these placements.

**Final fate:** Siegfried’s attempted mutual destruction does not kill Sorrento; he escapes. In Poseidon, Shun defeats him with Nebula Storm but spares him. Sorrento later helps Ikki destroy the North Atlantic Pillar, accompanies Julian Solo to aid flood victims, and appears in Hades to wish the Bronze Saints luck. He is one of the principal Marina survivors.

### Sea Dragon Kanon

Kanon’s Scale career is inseparable from his Gold-Saint identity and is discussed above in the Gold section. As Sea Dragon he commands the North Atlantic Pillar, uses Golden Triangle and Galaxian Explosion, manipulates Poseidon’s awakening, and directs the General conflict from behind the scenes. His Scale is abandoned when he accepts the Gemini Gold Cloth.

The manga has Kanon take Poseidon’s trident for Athena; the anime gives the blow to Seiya. Both versions preserve the larger outcome: Kanon recognizes his guilt, changes sides, and later sacrifices himself against Rhadamanthys.

### Poseidon, Julian Solo, and Thetis

#### Poseidon and Julian Solo

**Armor and role:** Julian Solo is Poseidon’s human vessel; Poseidon wears divine Scales and commands the Mariners.

**Power level:** Poseidon’s divine Cosmo is presented as vastly superior to human Cloth and Scale users. Even while only partially awakened, he returns attacks, destroys Bronze Cloths, and defeats Seiya, Shiryu, and Hyoga. His performance cannot be used to rank Marina Generals because he is the god they serve.

**Signature techniques:** Trident attacks, reflected Cosmo blasts, and divine control of the Underwater Sanctuary. The central weapon mechanism is the seven Pillars and the Main Breadwinner.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He is introduced in anime episode 100 and dominates episodes 110–114. In the manga he is awakened through Kanon’s manipulation and is eventually sealed by Athena.

**Final fate:** Athena seals Poseidon’s soul in the amphora and frees Julian Solo. In the Hades manga and anime, Poseidon briefly sends five Gold Cloths through the dimensional path to Elysium, showing that his hostility toward Athena does not prevent him from opposing Hades.

#### Mermaid Thetis

**Power level:** Thetis is a lower-ranking Marina commander, far below the Generals, but she has enough ability to delay or trap injured Bronze Saints.

**Signature techniques:** Coral Trap and mermaid-based aquatic attacks.

**Key appearances and arcs:** She appears in episodes 100–103, fights Seiya and Shaina, and guides the Bronze Saints toward the Pillars.

**Final fate:** She survives the Poseidon defeat and is shown swimming away after Julian is freed. The anime gives her a transformed mermaid ending; the exact manga endpoint is not established in the supplied material.

### Marina faction outcome

Baian, Io, Krishna, Caça, and Isaac die in the Pillar battles. Sorrento survives and becomes a neutral or benevolent survivor. Kanon redeems himself and dies fighting Rhadamanthys. Poseidon is sealed, Julian survives, the seven ocean Pillars and Main Breadwinner are destroyed, and Athena’s faction prevents the global flood.

## 6. Surplices: Specters and Hades’s faction

### The Underworld hierarchy

Hades commands 108 Specters, divided into Celestial and Terrestrial stars. Pandora functions as Hades’s chief administrator, while Thanatos and Hypnos are his true divine assistants. The Three Judges—Wyvern Rhadamanthys, Griffon Minos, and Garuda Aiacos—command the highest ordinary Specter tier.

The important limitation is that only a small upper echelon is consistently portrayed as Gold-Saint-level. The [Specters overview](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Specters) says that Hades created the 108 to rival Gold Saints, but only the highest-ranking Specters and a few just below them can match one. The distinction between Celestial and Terrestrial stars is not a reliable power hierarchy.

Hades Castle creates the most important environmental modifier in the classic story. Inside it, Mū, Aiolia, and Milo are reduced to ten percent of their normal power, while Rhadamanthys retains full strength. His domination of the three Gold Saints is therefore evidence of his superiority under that condition, not proof that he would defeat all three at full power.

### Wyvern Rhadamanthys

**Armor and rank:** Rhadamanthys wears the Wyvern Surplice and is one of the Three Judges. His standard star designation is the Celestial Fierce Star, though the Judge title is more useful for power comparison.

**Power level:** He is one of the strongest ordinary Specters. At Hades Castle he defeats Mū, Aiolia, and Milo in a three-on-one battle because their Cosmo is reduced to one-tenth. Outside that barrier, Kanon quickly gains the upper hand, showing that Rhadamanthys’s castle feat must remain conditional.

**Signature techniques:** Greatest Caution and powerful physical/energy attacks associated with the Wyvern Surplice.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episodes 117, 126–139 and in the corresponding manga Hades sequence. He is involved in Orphée’s death, fights Kanon, and commands the attack on Sanctuary.

**Final fate:** Kanon removes the Gemini Cloth, captures Rhadamanthys, and self-destructs with him. The anime modifies some earlier Seiya-and-Valentine staging but preserves the Kanon–Rhadamanthys mutual destruction. The [Rhadamanthys profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Wyvern_Rhadamanthys) documents the ten-percent castle condition.

### Griffon Minos

**Armor and rank:** Minos wears the Griffon Surplice and is one of the Three Judges, generally identified with the Celestial Noble Star.

**Power level:** Minos survives Hyoga’s Eighth Sense Aurora Execution and remains dangerous even after the Wailing Wall explosion. In the Hyperdimension, however, his body and Surplice are destroyed. The decisive factor is not simply Hyoga’s attack but the dimensional environment, which only Athena-blooded Final Cloths can safely cross.

**Signature techniques:** Cosmic Marionation, which controls the opponent’s body through invisible threads. The anime expands it so Minos can manipulate enemy techniques, reverse Seiya’s meteors, deflect Shun’s chains, and counter Hyoga and Shiryu.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episodes 131–140. The manga gives him the thread-based battle and Hyperdimension death; the anime adds several technique-control demonstrations.

**Final fate:** Minos survives the Wailing Wall explosion but is destroyed by the Hyperdimension while pursuing the Bronze Saints. The [Minos profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Griffon_Minos) explicitly labels the technique manipulation as anime material.

### Garuda Aiacos

**Armor and rank:** Aiacos wears the Garuda Surplice and is the third Judge, generally identified with the Celestial Heroic Star.

**Power level:** Aiacos initially overwhelms Ikki through speed, agility, and repeated attacks. Ikki adapts to the repeated rhythm of Garuda Flap and reverses Galactica Illusion with Phoenix Genma Ken, demonstrating the series’ rule that a technique loses effectiveness once an opponent truly understands it.

**Signature techniques:** Garuda Flap, Galactica Illusion, and Garuda-based aerial attacks.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episodes 131–134 and the corresponding manga chapters.

**Final fate:** Ikki defeats and kills him with Phoenix Hōyoku Tenshō or Flying Phoenix. *The Lost Canvas* uses a different Aiacos, whose human identity is Suikyō and whose story against Sisyphos must not be merged with the original Hades version. The [Aiacos profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Garuda_Aiacos) separates those continuities.

### Papillon Myu

**Armor and rank:** Myu wears the Papillon Surplice and carries the Terrestrial Charming Star.

**Power level:** Myu is one of the most dangerous non-Judge Specters. His metamorphic forms, telekinesis, and fairies nearly overwhelm Mū, and a secondary reference calls his psychokinesis the strongest among Specters, rivaling Mū’s. That qualitative statement is useful but not a universal numerical ranking.

**Signature techniques:** Ugly Eruption, Silky Thread, Fairy Thronging, and powerful psychokinesis.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He is sent with the Sanctuary assault force, appears in Hades episodes 121–122, and progresses through slime, larval, and final butterfly forms before confronting Mū. A reference identifies his first manga appearance as chapter 73, volume 20, and his anime appearance as episode 121.

**Final fate:** Mū traps Myu and his fairies inside Crystal Net and kills him with Starlight Extinction. The anime places Seiya nearby but reduces some of Myu’s psychokinetic display compared with the manga.

### Deep Niobe

**Armor and rank:** Niobe wears the Deep Surplice and carries the Terrestrial Darkness Star.

**Power level:** Niobe’s Deep Fragrance is lethal even to Aldebaran, but the apparent victory is tactically dependent. Aldebaran had destroyed his own eardrums against Sorrento and could not detect Niobe’s approach; Great Horn had already fatally damaged Niobe before the poison took effect.

**Signature techniques:** Deep Fragrance, a poisonous attack that invades the opponent’s senses and body.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episode 117 and in manga volume 19.

**Final fate:** Niobe attempts the same attack on Mū, but Crystal Wall blocks it. Mū recognizes that Niobe is already dead from Aldebaran’s delayed Great Horn; Niobe’s body then splits apart.

### Harpy Valentine

**Armor and rank:** Valentine wears the Harpy Surplice and carries the Celestial Wailing Star.

**Power level:** He is described as exceptionally powerful compared with many Specters faced by the Bronze Saints. In the manga he handles Seiya easily at the collapsing Hades Castle and later damages Seiya’s Cloth and removes Athena’s Cloth from his grasp.

**Signature techniques:** Greedy for Lives, which fires dozens of light-speed violet rays that consume life force, and Sweet Chocolate, which summons harpy spirits to throw and devour an opponent’s soul. The anime changes Greedy for Lives from a wing-driven attack to one fired through the fists.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episodes 135–137 and 140. The manga and anime significantly alter his first battle: the anime makes Seiya fight Rhadamanthys with the other Bronze Saints before facing Valentine later.

**Final fate:** In the manga, Athena’s Cloth ignites Seiya’s Cosmo and a single kick shatters Valentine’s Surplice and kills him. In the anime, the first attack destroys only the headpiece; Seiya finishes him with a Cosmos-charged Pegasus Meteor Fist. The [Valentine profile](https://saintseiya.fandom.com/wiki/Harpy_Valentine) documents both versions.

### Sphinx Pharaoh

**Armor and rank:** Pharaoh wears the Sphinx Surplice and is Hades’s personal musician, associated with the Celestial Beast or Divine Bestial Star.

**Power level:** Pharaoh is a specialized guardian rather than a Judge-level combatant. His musical and psychological techniques can threaten Seiya and Shun, but Orphée clearly surpasses him.

**Signature techniques:** Balance of Curse and harp-based musical attacks.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He guards the Second Prison in Hades episodes 130–131. Manga references supplied for him include volumes 23 and 24.

**Final fate:** Pharaoh uses Balance of Curse against Seiya and Shun, attempts to steal Athena’s Cloth with Pandora’s Mirror, and is killed by Orphée after his deception of Eurydice is exposed. *The Lost Canvas* gives him a separate role as the Gate Keeper of the Lost Canvas, where Sisyphos defeats him.

### Balrog Rune

**Armor and rank:** Rune wears the Balrog Surplice. His exact translated star title is not consistently established in the supplied material; he belongs to the higher administrative Specter tier rather than the Three Judges.

**Power level:** Rune’s strength is judicial and illusion-based. He can overwhelm Seiya psychologically by forcing him to confront his past actions and can use his Fire Whip to attack bodies and souls.

**Signature techniques:** Fire Whip and Reincarnation, which exposes a person’s past and assigns punishment.

**Key appearances and arcs:** He appears in Hades episodes 129–130, guarding the First Prison and Palace of Justice.

**Final fate:** Kanon uses illusion and manipulation against him, then destroys him with little difficulty. Manga chapter anchor unavailable.

### Other decisive Specters

#### Cyclops Giganto

Giganto is a high-ranking field commander in a Cyclops Surplice. He leads the Sanctuary assault group and fights Mū and Seiya in episode 121. His exact signature technique and star title are unavailable. Shaka kills him and the remaining lower Specters after exposing Saga, Camus, and Shura’s disguised identities.

#### Worm Raimi

Raimi wears the Worm Surplice and fights underground with binding tentacles. He traps Aiolia but is dragged above ground and killed by Lightning Bolt in episode 122. His individual ranking is below the Judges; an exact star title is unavailable.

#### Frog Zeros

Zeros is a minor Frog Specter who harasses the revived Gold Saints and Camus. Hyoga kills him with Aurora Execution in episode 127. No reliable power ranking or named technique beyond his Frog identity is supplied.

#### Acheron Charon

Charon guards the Acheron River and wears an Acheron Surplice. His Rolling Oar defends against attacks, while Eddying Current Crusher attacks from the river. Seiya defeats and kills him in Hades episode 128 after learning both techniques. His final fate is death; exact star rank is unavailable.

#### Lycaon Phlegyas

Phlegyas guards the swamp in the Fourth Prison. He defeats Hyoga and Shiryu briefly, but Kanon kills him with Galaxian Explosion in episode 132. His Surplice rank and precise star title are unavailable.

#### Ivan and Rock

Troll Ivan and Golem Rock are brief prison guardians in episode 131. Hyoga kills Ivan with Diamond Dust, and Shiryu kills Rock with Rising Dragon. Their armor, techniques beyond those attacks, and exact star titles are not established in the supplied evidence.

#### Queen, Gordon, and Sylphid

Alraune Queen, Minotauros Gordon, and Basilisk Sylphid are the final named Specters who confront Shiryu in Elysion. Shiryu kills all three with One Hundred Dragons in episode 140. Sylphid briefly survives the initial attack but is destroyed by Hyperdimension pressure while pursuing Shiryu. Individual power rankings and exact star titles are unavailable.

### Thanatos and Hypnos: divine Surplices

Thanatos and Hypnos are not ordinary Specters. Their Surplices are soaked in divine blood but are explicitly not true Kamui or God Cloths.

#### Thanatos

**Power level:** Thanatos is vastly above ordinary Cloth users and initially destroys five Bronze Cloths and five Gold Cloths in the anime. Even five Bronze Saints wearing Gold Cloths cannot hurt him. He is finally defeated only when Seiya’s Pegasus God Cloth awakens.

**Signature techniques:** Terrible Providence and long-range divine attacks.
